title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock: single pass tracking min price, max profit.
shortTitle: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock: Single Pass
keyPoints: Track two variables: the minimum price seen so far and the maximum profit seen so far.
For each day, compute the profit if sold today (today's price minus the running minimum) and update the best profit.
Initialise the best profit to zero, encoding the rule that you are not forced to trade at a loss.
The algorithm runs in O(n) time and O(1) space, replacing the naive O(n squared) all-pairs comparison.
Use BigDecimal for money calculations to avoid floating-point rounding errors.
This is the single-transaction version; multi-transaction and at-most-K variants require dynamic programming.

s1_definition.oneliner: Track the lowest price so far and the best sell-today-minus-lowest profit in one pass.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock** – find the maximum profit from one buy followed by one later sell.
- **Running minimum** – track the minimum price seen so far as you scan forward.
- **Profit calculation** – at each day, `profit = price[i] - minSoFar`; update `maxProfit` if larger.
- **No-loss encoding** – initialise `maxProfit` to zero so the answer is zero if prices only fall.
- **Complexity** – O(n) time, O(1) space, replacing the O(n squared) all-pairs approach.
- **Variant awareness** – this solves single-transaction only; multi-transaction needs DP.
s1_definition.analogy: Rajesh follows a share on the National Bank of India trading app and wants the most he could have made by buying on one day and selling on a later day. Walking through the days once, he remembers the cheapest price seen so far and on each day asks: if I had bought at that cheapest price and sold today, how much would I make? He keeps the biggest such gain.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock asks for the maximum profit from one buy and one later sell. The single-pass solution tracks two variables: the minimum price seen so far and the best profit seen so far. For each day, I compute the profit if I sold today against the cheapest earlier price and update the best, then I update the running minimum.

The design choice I always call out is initialising the best profit to zero, which means I am not forced to trade. If prices only fall, the answer is zero rather than a loss. I also clarify that this is the single-transaction version, since multi-transaction and at-most-K variants need DP.

For financial calculations, I use BigDecimal to keep money exact, comparing with compareTo and subtracting with the subtract method. The common mistake is updating the minimum before computing the profit, which allows buying and selling on the same day.

At the National Bank of India, I used this in Rajesh's trading app backtest, computing the best single buy-then-sell profit over a price window quickly and never suggesting a buy after a sell.

Remember one sentence: track the running minimum price, and at each day the profit is today's price minus that minimum.
